Q080-01.notes: Let u=2x, x=u/2: 4(u/2)^2-6(u/2)+1=u^2-3u+1. A divides whole expression by 2; B substitutes 2x for x; D only fixes x^2 term.

Q080-03.notes: 12/(x-2)>2 with x-2>0 gives x-2<6, so 2<x<8. Graphing confirms. B from >3 error; C reverses inequality; D ignores condition.

Q080-04.notes: x^2+3=(x+3)^2 gives 6x+9=3, so x=-1 (point (-1,4)). Easily graphed.

Q080-06.notes: Vertex x=4, y=c-16; on y=x: c-16=4, c=20.

Q080-09.notes: Let angle A=x. AD=BD gives angle ABD=x, so angle BDC=2x; BD=BC gives angle C=2x; AB=AC gives angle ABC=2x. x+2x+2x=180, x=36.
